stage1.impression: A moody, convincingly deep night view through a shopfront into a timber-and-concrete listening bar, with good warm pools of light, true verticals and a plausible 35 mm kerbside lens; the record wall, the beams and the pendant row read well. Up close it gives itself away as CG: the shopfront steel is a high-contrast grunge decal with white flecks, the glass carries ghostly tan double-exposure rectangles over the record wall, a blown white disc hangs in the glass, the floor is a smeary grey wash, and the altar pair is tiny and grey at 20 m, so nothing reads as the hero. As it stands it is a well-designed but fairly generic dark bar; the etched name and the dancing-woman lightbox, the two things that would make it a specific place from the kerb, are not legible.

blocking_9: The name etched into the glass must read at a glance from the kerb (it is invisible now: emission 0.0)
The frosted lightbox must show the fogged silhouette of the dancing woman, evenly lit, facing the lens closely enough to read
The shopfront's blackened steel must read as real near-black steel with a soft brownish patina and sharp edges, not a grunge texture with white flecks
Glass reflections must be one coherent, believable set (street side), with no ghost rectangles over the record wall and no clipped disc
EARF's altar pair must be read at a glance as the hero: bigger in frame, the smoked acrylic glowing, at lum_median >= 75
The floor must read as polished concrete at 1:1, with no smeared mottling and no grey wash from the street lamps

defects.what: Translucent tan rectangles laid over the record wall: glass reflections that read as a double exposure or a compositing error, not a believable reflection of the street
A blown white disc in the glass at ceiling height (25.7 % clipped), most likely a street lamp's reflection; it reads as a moon or a stray light
The shopfront's steel mullion has a high-contrast grunge texture with white flecks and peeling-paint blotches; it reads as a game texture, not blackened steel
The steel header and frame on the right have the same grunge decal; the panels are flat and repeat
The fluted/frosted panel shows a vertical brown-to-grey gradient and no silhouette; the lightbox's subject is unreadable
The pale frosted rectangle is seen almost edge-on; it reads as a blank light panel
The floor is a smeared, mottled grey wash (denoiser smear and a noisy roughness map) with the brightest pool at the glass, not in the room
The altar speakers are about 35 px wide, grey-white (r69 g59 b53), and no brighter than the timber around them; they do not read as tinted acrylic or as the hero
A full-height black post just left of centre cuts the room and the bar in two
The Dome pendants read as plain white shades, not smoked tinted acrylic with a frosted liner
The sill/plinth band is near black (median 11.6, 14.7 % crushed), with no detail
The top edge of the glass/frame is a thin grungy strip with no clear construction
